Healthcare / Plastic surgery

GEO for plastic surgery clinics

People compare plastic surgeons and clinics for a defined procedure, clinician expertise, surgical setting and the steps before and after treatment. I examine AI recommendations and their sources, checking whether surgical services are confused with cosmetic treatments or individual outcomes are overstated.

  • Separate aesthetic and reconstructive surgery intent groups
  • Verifiable surgeon, licensing and care-setting information
  • Careful handling of patient photographs and outcome claims

Selection barriers

Why before-and-after pictures cannot establish surgical quality

Images may be useful context, but provider selection also involves the procedure, qualifications, clinical setting and aftercare.

01

Surgery and cosmetology are conflated

Cosmetic injections, reconstructive procedures and elective plastic surgery involve different services and care requirements. Broad advertising labels can obscure the actual authorised activity.

02

Photographic outcomes lack context

Before-and-after images vary with timing, camera angle and personal characteristics. Their use requires permission and scrutiny for misleading generalisations.

03

Published prices omit stages

The surgical fee may not cover assessment, tests, anaesthesia, inpatient care and follow-up. These should be described according to the provider's actual terms.

Verifiable facts

Evidence to verify before claiming a plastic surgery specialty

I assess licensed services, clinician profiles and the actual setting for each intervention. Russian Health Ministry Order 298n governs plastic surgery care; citing it does not prove a particular clinic is compliant. Informed consent requirements under Healthcare Act 323-FZ remain separate from promotional copy.

  • Authorised work at each site, qualified surgeons, consultation pathways and operating conditions
  • Procedure scope, assessment, anaesthesia, inpatient arrangements, follow-up and transparent prices
  • Lawful and permissioned photographs, accurate dates, suitable descriptions and no guaranteed outcome claims

This sector GEO methodology does not assert GAEO client performance in plastic surgery or any clinical treatment result.

Scope of work

How I would run plastic surgery GEO

The audit segments surgical intent, checks provider evidence and tracks whether the correct specialists are recommended.

  1. 01

    Procedure-based baseline

    Separate aesthetic and reconstructive intent, location and named-surgeon searches from unbranded recommendations.

  2. 02

    Verify provider information

    Review licences, clinician roles, procedure scope, actual fees and rights to use images.

  3. 03

    Publish substantiated service pages

    Prepare briefs for procedures, real surgeons, surgical conditions, questions and non-promissory care explanations.

  4. 04

    Recheck recommendation quality

    Measure BMR, citations and errors, especially overpromised outcomes or outdated clinician affiliations.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can surgical and cosmetic services share a website section?+

They may share navigation, but the services, qualifications and applicable requirements must remain distinct. A surgical procedure should not be marketed as a simple cosmetic treatment.

Can before-and-after pictures support GEO?+

Only with appropriate legal permissions and accurate context. One patient's photographs cannot establish the likely outcome for another.

Can a clinic guarantee no complications?+

No. Medical risks belong in clinical consultation and consent processes. Marketing content should not promise the absence of complications.

What should a quoted procedure fee include?+

State whether consultation, tests, anaesthesia, admission and follow-up are included. Different quotes are not comparable without this breakdown.

What are GAEO's plastic surgery GEO fees?+

The published GAEO plans apply. Scope depends on surgical disciplines, physicians, practice locations and the baseline prompt set.
